correctness.rationale: In a tree each target is reached precisely when its unique source-to-target path is open. Summing the path probabilities including the empty path gives the stated distance-histogram polynomial, even at p=0 and p=1. Polynomial identity on the interval is equivalent to matching all coefficients. Rooted isomorphism of two markings in one tree is exactly membership in one automorphism orbit. The supplied rooted-code construction is exhaustive by the multiset decomposition at the root, and minimizing that code over roots gives a complete free-tree invariant. The independent calculation uses leaf extensions (deleting a leaf gives a predecessor of every nontrivial tree), canonical one- or two-center decompositions, and rooted shapes for the orbits. It reproduces all order totals, no colliding orbit pairs up to nine, and exactly two at ten in different free-tree classes. Independently of the package's mask enumeration, multiplying integer component-size polynomials over child branches reproduces both exact laws and moments: first-moment numerators 1488 and 1920, respectively, and second-moment numerators (6032,6116) and (9120,9088) in the labelled witness order, all over 512. Equal means leave signed variance gaps -21/128 and +1/16 in that order. One variance measurement therefore separates exactly the cases not already separated by the curve.
residual_risks: No statement is established for larger trees, for unknown graphs, or for finite/noisy estimates of the curve and variance.

value.rationale: The problem asks what a standard graph invariant can recover up to unavoidable symmetry in a fixed graph. The least failure order, complete list there and exact rescue by one second-moment statistic give reusable minimal obstructions and benchmarks for comparing graph invariants. The coalescence is equality of the whole polynomial, not a single accidental numeric tie or a repeat of tree-count tables.
residual_risks: Exact inference on very small known trees is the value established, not robustness, large-network inference, or any claim about a real pathogen.
